body.x: TESOLLO Inc. (CEO Young-jin Kim) participated in the “HUMANOID M.AX Alliance” pavilion at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

TESOLLO develops and produces the multi-joint robotic hand “Delto Gripper Series,” which realizes human-level delicate manipulation, and provides high-precision gripper solutions required for the humanoid robot field.

Delto Gripper products have gained recognition for both market viability and technical excellence and are now applied in real-world applications at global conglomerates. Major research institutions such as Stanford University, ETH Zurich, KAIST, and National Taiwan University use the products as platforms for advanced robotics research. In addition, TESOLLO operates a stable global sales and distribution network through 14 overseas agencies and plans to expand into more countries.

At CES 2026, TESOLLO presented an integrated demo that combined its five-finger multi-joint robot gripper, Delto Gripper 5F (DG-5F), with the upper-body humanoid robot Adam. As a result, the company implemented a humanoid-robotic solution capable of performing precise grasping and manipulation of unstructured objects.

DG-5F is a high-function multi-joint robot gripper with a total of 20 degrees of freedom, precisely mimicking the structure of the human hand to stably grasp and delicately manipulate objects of various shapes. Based on a structure in which each finger operates independently, the gripper enables manipulation-centered task execution beyond simple grasping. TESOLLO explained that these characteristics make the gripper suitable for applications that require human-like hand movements, such as precision assembly, teleoperation, and simulation environments.

The company also applied a direct-drive actuation method and high-resolution magnetic encoders to enhance control performance, while a modular design improved maintainability and productivity, earning high trust from both industrial sites and research institutions.

body.cap: An exhibition view of TESOLLO’s five-finger multi-joint robot gripper, Delto Gripper 5F (DG-5F). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In the exhibition demo, the humanoid equipped with DG-5F and a 3D vision camera recognized poly-bags inside a box and performed pick-and-place tasks. The setup also included a peg-in-hole demo that allowed visitors to confirm precise hand manipulation, going beyond simple object transfer. Through this, TESOLLO demonstrated the solution's expandability into full humanoid-robot applications.

A TESOLLO official said, “We participated to expand product supply references in overseas markets and to enhance brand awareness of the Delto Gripper,” adding, “We aim to directly introduce product performance and application possibilities through live demos and use cases on site, while discovering new customers and partners. We also plan to explore collaboration opportunities through meetings with robot manufacturers, system integrators, and research institutions, and to strengthen our sales and distribution networks in major markets, including North America.”

TESOLLO plans to continue expanding sales of its existing flagship products, DG-5F, DG-4F, and DG-3F-M, while broadening its product lineup through the full-scale market launch of new products, DG-1F and DG-2F. Through this strategy, the company aims to respond more flexibly to diverse customer needs and application areas.

body.cap: Visitors at CES 2026 observe TESOLLO’s integrated demo combining the five-finger multi-joint robot gripper Delto Gripper 5F (DG-5F) and the upper-body humanoid robot Adam. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: On the export front, TESOLLO plans to maintain stable sales in major markets based on its existing overseas customers and partners, while gradually expanding into new countries and regions. The company identified the United States, Europe, and Japan as key target markets with strong demand for humanoid robots and advanced robotics technologies.

Looking ahead, TESOLLO plans to further expand its overseas agency network to strengthen local sales and technical support capabilities and to establish a more efficient sales and distribution structure. Through overseas exhibitions and collaborations with local partners, the company aims to continuously identify market needs and incorporate them into product improvements and new product development, gradually strengthening its competitiveness in the global market.

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
